clue.text: Ant's one person employed by local council …

definitions.meaning: an ant is a social insect that works, so cryptically it is one of these
a council officer who supports vulnerable families and individuals

explanation.surface: The clue trails off into the next one, setting up a sentence about Ant of the TV duo Ant and Dec having a council job.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 9 across, where Dec appears: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Councils employ caseworkers in their care services; a worker ant in a colony is, punningly, a social labourer.

clue.text: Make a choice — the compiler's is electronic to get best result

parts.note: to opt is to choose
the setter refers to themself as I, so 'the compiler is' becomes I'M
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: The setter's choice is electronic, aiming for top results.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve something as far as possible is to make it perform at its peak.

clue.text: Game is heartlessly petty

indicators.note: with its middle cut out, only the outer letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a game as small-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's guessing pastime, 'something beginning with...', is a familiar car game.

clue.text: Novel a lone donor broadcast

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An anonymous benefactor's novel is aired on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: R. D. Blackmore's 1869 romance set on Exmoor is named after its heroine.

clue.text: Dull alumnus cooked suet

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: cooked material is altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former student prepared a stodgy suet dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow-witted or blunt; both senses of the adjective match.

clue.text: Family of helpful socialist

parts.note: kind means helpful or considerate
red is a common label for a left-winger

explanation.surface: A family belonging to a well-meaning leftie.
explanation.definitionFit: One's relatives or kin; the word works as noun for blood relations.

clue.text: Note vulgar perfume breaking out once more

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
crude means vulgar
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: A message about a tacky fragrance that keeps flaring up.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of diseases or trouble recurring after a dormant spell, so the adjective describes a renewed outbreak.

clue.text: Criticise a graduate's hat

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: Someone running down a graduate's headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimmed straw hat, the plaited type named after the Central American country.

clue.text: … Dec's place in regular series to continue

definitions.meaning: Dec is December, which comes at the end of the run of months
to go on or endure, as in 'the food won't hold out'

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 across, it seems to discuss where Dec stands in the regular billing of the TV duo Ant and Dec.
explanation.walkthrough: Dec looks like the presenter of Ant and Dec (a British TV duo, Dec always named second), but here it is the abbreviation for December.
explanation.definitionFit: December closes the calendar year; separately, to endure or go on is a verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: Original computer department in terror of extreme morality

indicators.note: one pair of pieces is placed inside the word for terror

parts.note: terror is panic
the prefix ur- means original or primitive, as in Urtext
IT, information technology, is a firm's computer department

explanation.surface: An office scene: the founding IT team in a state of fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritans were noted for strict moral and religious standards, so the adjective describes rigid, severe morals.

clue.text: Not showing total belief, partner avoids church as the done thing?

indicators.note: the word for belief is not shown in full; its final letter drops

parts.note: faith is belief

indicators.note: the partner keeps clear of the church abbreviation, so it is removed

parts.note: an accomplice is a partner in crime
CE is Church of England

explanation.surface: A partner skips church, lacking full faith, and calls that the proper behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The done thing' usually means good form; here the question mark flags a literal reading: something already done.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means an accomplished fact, something settled before anyone can object.

clue.text: Sad to say, gripping marine excursions often accompany these

indicators.note: the expression of regret holds the other piece within it

parts.note: alas is a cry meaning sad to say
RM stands for Royal Marine(s)

explanation.surface: A regretful note that a sea trip has a grip on travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alarms and excursions' is an old Shakespearean stage direction for battle noise and movement, now an idiom for confused activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage directions pair the two words in a fixed phrase meaning noisy skirmishing, so these warnings come with excursions.

clue.text: Woman of Munich, say, beginning to hoard gold, succeeded with French gold

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word that follows is used

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A Bavarian woman starts stashing gold and makes her fortune with French gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for a housewife, used in English; Munich is in Germany, and 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Stout sailor left in old folks' institution — that can be understood

parts.note: fat means stout

indicators.note: the sailor and the abbreviation for left go inside the care facility

parts.note: a home is a residence for elderly people
AB is able seaman

explanation.surface: A plump sailor left in a care home for the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to the bottom of something is to grasp it, so the adjective means comprehensible.

clue.text: Refurbished material from altar's torn, this person explains

indicators.note: renovated material is remade, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A church restorer reusing fabric from a ripped altar cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An interpreter of foreign text renders its meaning in another language, which is a kind of explaining.

clue.text: Tool that cuts and increases, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for increases is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: to increase is to add, so increases gives adds

explanation.surface: Talk of a cutting tool that also boosts something.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an axe-like woodworking implement with its blade at right angles, used to shape timber.

clue.text: Joker, willing to participate, settled in carriage

parts.note: a wag is a joker
if you're on, you're up for joining in
lit means alighted or settled, as a bird does

explanation.surface: A prankster happy to join in sits down in a railway compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sleeping car on Continental trains, from French for bed wagon.

clue.text: Drink repels a couturière

indicators.note: pushing away the article removes it from the hot drink

parts.note: cocoa is a hot chocolate drink

explanation.surface: A fashion designer turns away a glass someone offers her.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco Chanel was the celebrated French dressmaker, a couturière being a female fashion designer.

clue.text: I should abandon unfinished heavenly instrument

indicators.note: the letter I is to leave, being taken out
the word for heavenly loses its last letter

parts.note: celestial means heavenly

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to give up an incomplete heavenly instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the final L of CELESTIAL; 'should abandon' then removes the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument with hammers striking metal plates, used in Tchaikovsky's Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

clue.text: Spectral tailless rodents seen by parking area in southern county

indicators.note: places the rodents' piece next to the rest

parts.note: P is the map symbol for parking

indicators.note: the abbreviation for area is set inside the county name

parts.note: Hants is the short form of Hampshire, a county in southern England

indicators.note: the rodents lose their final letter

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: Ghostly docked-tail mice glimpsed beside a car park somewhere in the south of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Phantasms are ghosts or illusions, so the adjective means ghostly, like a spectre.

clue.text: Change government department providing yachts primarily

parts.note: MoD is the Ministry of Defence
if means providing, as a condition

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A ministry might alter its stance if it supplies boats.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter or adjust something is a plain synonym.

clue.text: One that's mounted on horse goes off south, heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, the south letter climbs to the top

parts.note: addles means goes rotten, as eggs do

explanation.surface: A rider mounts a horse that sets off south, then turns north.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat strapped onto a horse's back is fitted, or mounted, upon it.

clue.text: Bribe, perhaps, to get trees

definitions.meaning: to 'grease' or lubricate someone's hands is to pay them off
tropical trees grown for their oil-rich fruit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that the phrase is a playful version of 'grease palms', a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying someone off is greasing their hand; separately, these are plantation trees whose fruit yields cooking oil.

clue.text: Turf next to study is very wet

indicators.note: places the turf beside the study

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a small study or private room

explanation.surface: Grass laid beside a home office is waterlogged.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through or saturated is a standard synonym.

clue.text: Catch present being delivered

indicators.note: a speech delivered is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: here means present, as in a register

explanation.surface: Someone catches a gift as it arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch what someone says is to make it out by ear.

clue.text: Booed pals dancing this

indicators.note: letters that dance move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Friends being jeered while they perform a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the jeered friends are doing this dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-style ballroom dance modelled on the march of a bullfight.

clue.text: Chasm turning out cold and deserted

indicators.note: throwing out the abbreviation for cold removes it from the chasm

parts.note: a cleft is a split or chasm
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A gorge that turned out cold and empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned, as in having been gone from; past tense of leave.

clue.text: Arty imbecile could make this programme

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: A dig at a reality show: a pretentious fool could produce it.
explanation.walkthrough: The British reality TV show 'I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!' is hosted by Ant and Dec, as in 1 and 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a long-running British TV show set in the jungle.
